articles.title: US stocks hold near records on hopes of an agreement with Iran
articles.description: Stocks held close to their records on Wall Street, while oil prices held steady. The S&P 500 slipped 0.2% Wednesday from the all-time high it set a day earlier. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.5%, and the Nasdaq composite lost 0.8%. SpaceX sank after increasing its spending on artificial intelligence. The Walt Disney Co. rose after reporting results that beat analysts’ forecasts, helped by “Toy Story 5.” European markets were mixed and Asian markets closed higher. Treasury yields slipped in the bond market. The price of Brent crude was little changed at about $79 a barrel.

articles.title: US-Iran War Live: Iran rejects foreign mediation on Hormuz, no new US talks despite outreach
articles.description: US-Iran War News Live Updates: Iran has stepped up diplomatic efforts to avert another round of US strikes, warning Gulf states that any attack on its territory would trigger retaliation against energy infrastructure, oil facilities and US-linked assets across the region, reported Reuters. Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi urged Saudi Arabia, Qatar and other regional partners to press Washington towards diplomacy, while Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman reportedly asked US President Donald Trump to delay military action and revive negotiations. Trump later said talks were "moving along nicely" but warned Iran would be hit "really hard" if diplomacy failed. Even as Tehran denied formal peace talks, it confirmed progress with Oman on a proposed framework to manage shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints. The proposed arrangement could give Iran greater oversight of ships entering the Gulf, although key disagreements remain. Markets reacted cautiously, with hopes of de-escalation weighing on oil prices, while continued shipping risks kept traders on edge. Tensions remained high after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis claimed fresh attacks on Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, adding to concerns over global energy supplies and regional stability. Follow IndiaToday.in for live updates.

articles.title: linked proposal is well worth a try
articles.description: IT’s an alarming paradox: in a country which records over 500 road mishap deaths every day, about 56 per cent of the registered motor vehicles are operating without mandatory insurance. The scale of non-compliance points to major lapses in enforcing the Motor Vehicles Act. No wonder the Supreme Court has taken a serious note of the matter. It has asked the Centre to try out a pilot project under which fuel can be denied at petrol pumps in the absence of valid insurance.

articles.title: Iran says Oman transit route viable for 2-4 months; US MOU return required
articles.description: Iran conditions the viability of an Oman-proposed Strait of Hormuz transit route on US adherence to the Islamabad MOU, estimating a 2-4 month window. This adds complexity to US efforts to reopen the waterway without fees, amidst volatile oil prices and divergent diplomatic stances.
